title: Specialization and Coordination
description: Build multi-agent systems where each agent has a role, shares context, agrees on tasks, and reports results up to a central coordinator.

data.text: In a multi-agent system, agents are typically specialized by role — researcher, analyst, writer, reviewer — each with a dedicated capability set. Tasks are decomposed and assigned to the agent best suited to handle them. Agents exchange messages (or structured summaries) to keep coordination efficient.
The classic pattern is an orchestrator (dispatcher) that breaks the high-level goal into subtasks, assigns them to workers, collects outputs, then synthesizes a final answer.

rows: Hard to recover from failure mid-task
Failures in one specialist don't break others

data.question: You need a full PR review: it includes research on conventions, drafting the diff, writing coverage tests, and proposing a release note. Which combination of subtasks best fits a multi-agent workflow, and why not as one agent?
data.answer: Specialize into three agents: Researcher (explore conventions), Draftsman (write diff + tests), Reviewer (release notes). Coordinating four tools across specialists gives better error isolation, faster parallel work, and clearer ownership; a single agent forces it to absorb all failure modes.
